# `sandloom.sdk.projections`

Query projections: the declarative `Projection` and today's descriptors
and helpers.

Public API 1.0 (spec §2.2, Appendix C). A name whose mechanism lands at a
later hand-off raises `NotImplementedError` naming it.

`from sandloom.sdk.projections import <name>`. Signatures in a terminal: `sandloom docs <name>`. Beginner names are the ones generated code and the examples use; any other name is advanced (mark its import line `# sandloom: advanced <reason>` in generated code and examples).

#### `ConsistencyToken.wait_for`

```python
async def wait_for(
    self,
    projection: str,
    stored_version: Callable[[str, str], Awaitable[int | None]],
    *,
    wait_ms: int | None = None,
    refresh: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | None = None,
) -> bool
```

Poll `stored_version(digest, group)` (the row's value of that
group's version column) until `projection` reached every entry, at
most `wait_ms` (default `PROJECTION_RYW_WAIT_MS`); `False` when
the budget ran out (serve stale, never an error). `refresh` runs
before every round but the first (a caller polling cached rows
rereads them there).

### `monotonic_delete`

```python
async def monotonic_delete(
    session: AsyncSession,
    target: Any,
    *,
    key: dict[str, Any],
    version_column: str,
    incoming_version: int,
    values: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    insert_only: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    deleted_column: str = 'deleted_at',
    deleted_at: datetime | None = None,
) -> bool
```

Persist a versioned tombstone, including when deletion arrives first.

A physical DELETE discards the version and lets a delayed older upsert
resurrect the row. This helper retains it using the same tenant/version
checks as `monotonic_upsert`. The projection needs a nullable timestamp
`deleted_column` and reads must filter it to NULL. `values` and
`insert_only` must supply tenant_id and other required columns so an
absent row can be inserted as a tombstone. Only an explicitly newer event
can subsequently clear it by upserting `deleted_column=None`.

Tombstones must survive at least the complete replay/rebuild horizon;
removing them early reintroduces resurrection. Rebuilders apply source
versions through the same helper and must not infer deletion from an
incomplete source listing.

### `monotonic_update`

```python
async def monotonic_update(
    session: AsyncSession,
    target: Any,
    *,
    match: dict[str, Any],
    values: dict[str, Any],
    version_column: str,
    incoming_version: int,
) -> int
```

Update every projection row matching `match`, guarded by source version.

For denormalised fields that fan out across many rows (e.g. a project's name
copied onto every task row): updates the matched rows whose stored
`version_column` is strictly older than `incoming_version` (or NULL),
setting the new `values` and version. Out-of-order/duplicate project
events are no-ops. Returns the number of rows updated. Auto-scoped to the
bound tenant (if any) on tenant-owned tables — see the module docstring.

Note: this only refreshes rows that ALREADY EXIST and are COMMITTED (or
locked by this transaction). A row another writer inserted but has not
committed yet is invisible here, so a writer that reads the source over RPC
and then inserts can lose this update for good. Serialise the two writers on
a local, version-guarded snapshot row of the source (upsert it here first;
`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` it in the other writer and copy its values) — see
the projecthub taskboard `ProjectSnapshot`.

### `monotonic_upsert`

```python
async def monotonic_upsert(
    session: AsyncSession,
    target: Any,
    *,
    key: dict[str, Any],
    values: dict[str, Any],
    version_column: str,
    incoming_version: int,
    insert_only: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> bool
```

Insert-or-update a single projection row, guarded by source version.

Inserts the row (`key` + `values` + `insert_only` + the version) when
absent; on a primary-key/unique conflict it updates `values` and the
version ONLY when the stored `version_column` is strictly older than
`incoming_version` (or NULL). A duplicate (equal version) or an
out-of-order older event leaves the row untouched. Returns `True` when a
row was inserted or updated.

`insert_only` columns are written on INSERT but NEVER touched by the
on-conflict update — for fields this source merely SEEDS but does not own
(e.g. a task upsert seeds the denormalised project name once, but project
events, guarded by their own version, are the authority for keeping it
fresh). Without this, every task update would clobber project fields back to
whatever the seed lookup returned, rolling back fresher project data.

### `Projection`

```python
class Projection(
    name: str,
    *,
    key: tuple[str, ...],
    groups: Sequence[SourceGroup],
    model: type[TenantScoped] | None = None,
    store: tuple[str, str] | None = None,
    insert_only: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    deleted_column: str = 'deleted_at',
    rebuild_from: BoundContractMethod | tuple[str, str] | None = None,
    lag_slo_s: float = 5.0,
    at_least_once: bool = False,
) -> None
```

A declared read model (spec §6.4), registered by `define_module`
from the module's `projections` submodule.

`model=` (a relational `TenantScoped` table) is the supported target
in 1.0. `store=` (a `document_store` instance) is experimental in 1.0:
tested against the in-memory driver only, without production drivers.

### `ProjectionConsumerDescriptor`

```python
class ProjectionConsumerDescriptor(
    name: str,
    source_channel: str,
    projection: str,
    handler: ProjectionHandler,
    durable: bool = True,
    required: bool = True,
    module: str | None = None,
    group: str | None = None,
    start_from: str = 'earliest',
    bind_tenant_from: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

A durable consumer that applies one source channel to one projection.

The durable consumer-group id on the event bus is `group_name`
(`<module>:<name>` when registered through `ModuleAPI`; the module is
stamped by the loader): each consumer gets its OWN group, so it has its own
pending list, redelivery and dead-letter queue, independent of every other
subscriber to the channel. Keep `name` stable across deploys — changing it
makes the bus treat the consumer as brand new (a new group starting at
`start_from`, default the channel's retained backlog). `group` pins an
explicit group id instead.

`durable` (default) claims each event id in the handler's Unit of Work
(`UNIQUE(consumer, event_id)`) so the apply runs exactly once even though
delivery is at-least-once; idempotent handlers may set it `False` and rely
on the monotonic upsert alone.

`required=True` makes the projection subscription part of readiness. Use
`False` only when the owning read path explicitly tolerates a stale or
unavailable projection.

#### `ProjectionConsumerDescriptor.group_name`

```python
group_name  (property)
```

The durable consumer-group id (also the exactly-once inbox key).

### `ProjectionRebuilder`

```python
class ProjectionRebuilder(Protocol)
```

Reconstructs a projection from its source modules (idempotently).

Every method rebuilds a SCOPE and returns a
`ProjectionRebuildResult`. Implementations re-read source state via
public contracts/events and apply it through the same monotonic upsert the
live consumers use, so a rebuild and steady-state delivery converge to the
same rows. Rebuilds must be safe to run while consumers are live. Source
deletions require versioned tombstones (`monotonic_delete`), never
physical DELETEs: a stale source row observed before a concurrent delete
must not resurrect a row during the rebuild. Retain tombstones through
the whole replay/rebuild horizon and distinguish complete snapshots from
partial listings before reconciling absent entities.

### `ProjectionView`

```python
class ProjectionView(Generic)(
    projection: Projection,
    row: type[R],
    session: Any,
    *,
    on_stale: Literal['serve', 'source'] = 'serve',
    wait_ms: int | None = None,
    token: ConsistencyToken | None = None,
    response: Response | None = None,
) -> None
```

Reads one projection (`Annotated[ProjectionView[R], View(...)]`).

Rows whose tombstone is set are never returned. With a consistency token
(`SANDLOOM-Consistency-Token`) a read waits up to `wait_ms` for the rows
the caller's write produces; then it serves anyway with `stale = True`
and `SANDLOOM-Projection-Stale: true` (`on_stale="serve"`), or reads the
entity from its source through `rebuild_from` (`on_stale="source"`,
`get` only). Never an error status.

### `QueryProjectionDescriptor`

```python
class QueryProjectionDescriptor(
    name: str,
    owner_module: str,
    version: str = 'v1',
    source_events: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    storage: str = 'default',
    consistency: Literal['eventual'] = 'eventual',
    rebuildable: bool = True,
    purge: TombstonePurger | None = None,
    token_entries: TokenEntries | None = None,
) -> None
```

A denormalised cross-module read model owned by one module.

`consistency` is intentionally fixed to `"eventual"`: a projection lags
its source modules by the event delivery + apply time and must never back a
strong-consistency command invariant (validate those against the owner's
public command contract instead). `rebuildable` records that the
projection can be dropped and reconstructed from the source modules — the
projection is a cache, not a source of truth.

#### `QueryProjectionRegistry.snapshot`

```python
def snapshot(self) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]
```

Shallow copy of the maps for a later `restore`.

Descriptors are frozen/immutable and rebuilders are opaque objects, so a
shallow per-map copy is enough to rewind a failed module registration
without leaking later mutations into the snapshot.

#### `QueryProjectionRegistry.restore`

```python

```

Reset the maps to a prior `snapshot`.

### `start_projection_consumers`

```python
async def start_projection_consumers(
    core: CoreFacade,
    *,
    session_opener: SessionOpener | None = None,
) -> int
```

Subscribe every registered projection consumer to the event bus.

Returns the number of consumers wired through the canonical supervised
runtime. Duplicate groups and missing required projections fail startup;
repeated calls do not add duplicate handlers. `session_opener` defaults
to `unit_of_work.db_session` and is injectable for tests.
